_README: The script for this app's 'how to turn off analytics' video. Read by the shared scripts in the
`iboalali-apps` kit; see the `store-video` skill for the full shape and what each step verb does.
Its takes and cuts are filed under the storyboard's own path below Play Store/Video, so it cannot
write over the promo or the other how-to: raw/howto/analytics/<orientation>/<locale>/ and
Worth more than it sounds for an app in this corner of Android. People who root their phones tend
to care what leaves them, and the app has two answers rather than one: a switch that stops the
sending, and a reset that severs what was already sent from anything sent later.
_locales: English only for now. Nothing here is a framework surface, so localeScope is 'app' and every
extra language is one caption set plus one `--locale <name>` run: no rootable image, no reboot.

_note: The promo's, unchanged. Taken from the launcher icon, which is the app's only real brand mark:
a white '#' on Material Deep Purple 500. See the promo storyboard for why it is deliberately
NOT the app's Material theme.

_zoom: Two levels, as in the other how-to. The pushes go on the two settings rows the video names, so
their second lines are readable: those lines are the ones that say what the control actually
does, and this video is about a privacy promise rather than a button.

_package: The DEBUG build, like the promo: the armed root result is BuildConfig.DEBUG-gated and no
emulator is rooted, so there is no other way to film this state.
That has a cost worth knowing before re-recording. `app/src/debug/res` renames the app to
'Basic Root Checker (Debug)' and overrides the splash drawable, and the title bar renders
app_name, so the resource overrides have to be neutralized on disk for the build being filmed:
The applicationId keeps its .debug suffix, which is invisible: nothing this journey films
_startInApp: No demo_root here: this video never runs a check, so the status area stays on its 'touch the #
button' prompt, which is what a viewer's own first screen looks like.
demo_device_name and demo_device_model decide what the device card says. Without them it reads
'emulator' and 'emu64xa', which contradicts the Pixel bezel the capture is composited into.
Arming a device also tells the app a recording is in progress, which is what hides Settings'
debug-only 'Debug: record products' card from the bottom of the list this video films.

_note: The promo's bed. The same track across an app's videos is what makes them read as a set.
1300ms is a beat to read the screen before anything moves. The push goes to the control
about to be tapped, so the camera move and the press are one gesture.
Still zoomed from the previous scene, which is the point: the menu opens under the control
we pushed in on, so the item being named is legible. The pull-back rides the push
transition to Settings, so the camera and the app move together instead of taking turns.
Reset first, switch second, and the order is forced by the app rather than chosen: the
reset row only exists while analytics are on. Turning the switch off first would make the
row this scene needs disappear before it could be filmed.
The pull-back rides the dialog opening. It has to happen: the dialog is centred while the
camera is pushed in on a row, and at 2.0x the horizontal cut is narrower than the dialog,
so holding the push would crop it.
The trailing wait covers the confirmation snackbar.
The switch flips and the reset row below it disappears, because there is no identity left
to reset once nothing is being sent. That is the scene's payoff and it needs no caption: a
row vanishing says 'this no longer applies' better than a sentence would.
The trailing 1100ms is the tail the end card fades in over. The pull-back has to finish and
settle before the take stops, because the recording is frozen on its LAST frame.
The promo's card, unchanged. Same app, same offer, same link.
